target_customer: Direct-to-consumer e-commerce brands (Shopify based) and their growth and marketing teams
problem: After iOS signal loss, DTC brands could not trust ad attribution and spent heavy manual effort buying and scaling ads.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for marketing measurement, tracking and agentic media buying
product_category: Marketing attribution and AI ad-buying agents

founders.name: Jan-Henrik Lambrechts
founders.background_notes: YC page: worked on ML vision models at Tsinghua University; education not listed.

founders.name: Thomas Holvoet
education: Left a data science master's at Columbia to start Converge

technical_complexity.rationale: Server-side tracking, identity resolution and multi-touch attribution across ad platforms is real data engineering; later agentic buying added LLM work.

defensibility.rationale: Tracking pixels and ad-account integrations are replicable, but embedded tracking and first-party data pipelines are sticky once installed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Triple Whale and Northbeam were established in DTC attribution; Converge's own comparison pages position against them. No source on any acquisition of or copy by them was found.

market_need_then: iOS tracking changes left DTC brands with unreliable attribution; third-party comparison pieces describe this as the reason Triple Whale and Northbeam grew, though those pieces are recent.

identity.voice_and_tone: Product-led, metric-heavy claims such as $2.4B ad spend optimized; tagline 'The AI-native growth platform for DTC'.

brand_strength.rationale: A separate company, Converge Digital, sells agentic media buying under a near-identical name, and no brand-focused press was found.

pivots.from: Marketing measurement and attribution for B2C
pivots.to: AI agents that buy and scale ads
pivots.why: The YC page and site now describe agentic media buying as the lead product; no source gives a date or stated reason.

outcome_analysis: Converge is active with named customers including Hims & Hers and a claimed $2.4B in optimized ad spend. It raised a $5.6M seed in February 2025, about a year and a half after the batch, and has moved from attribution toward agentic ad buying where Hims & Hers cites the agent making over 90% of Meta budget changes (a vendor-published claim). No acquisition or layoff news was found.
notes: Round amount: Axios says $5.6M, lavx says $5.7M; Axios used. The investor list (YC, General Catalyst) comes from search summaries of the lavx article and was not opened in full. A Hims & Hers case study on the company site is vendor-written. Founding year 2022 per YC page. Competitors left empty: comparison pages are 2025 to 2026. The Axios article is paywalled so only its headline-level data was seen via search.
